memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites. After that, you will be gathered to your people." So Moses said to the people, "Arm some of your men to go to war against the Midianites so that they may carry out the Lord's vengeance on them." - Num 31:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before we read a single line of this chapter, we must hold it steady in its own moment. Back in Numbers 25, Midian had deliberately led Israel into sexual sin and idol worship at Peor, and a plague killed twenty-four thousand people. This was not a random neighbour; this was a nation that set out to destroy God's people spiritually. What we read here is not Moses' private grudge but God's judicial reckoning against a specific people at a specific point in redemptive history.

Notice the word "vengeance." In our mouths that word usually means wounded pride lashing out. But this is the Lord's vengeance, not Israel's. Justice belongs to God, and here He was acting as the righteous Judge of the whole earth. Moses himself was told he would die soon after — even the leader was not above God's timing.

We live under a different covenant. Jesus told His followers to love their enemies and leave vengeance to God (Rom 12:19). The cross is where God's justice and mercy meet: our sin was judged fully in Christ, so we are freed from repaying evil ourselves. This chapter reminds us that God takes sin seriously — seriously enough to judge it, and seriously enough to bear it Himself at Calvary.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it change this passage to see the judgment as God's, not human revenge?
2. Where are you tempted to take vengeance into your own hands?
3. How does the cross satisfy your longing for justice?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Righteous God, You alone judge rightly, and I thank You that in Christ my sin was judged and my debt was paid. Help me to release my grievances to You and to love even those who wrong me. Amen.
